gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 15?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 15 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent weather model consensus from sources including the German Weather Service and international forecasts has positioned Munich's August 15 high near 34–35°C under predominantly sunny, stable high-pressure conditions with light winds and minimal cloud cover, driving near-certain trader alignment on the 35°C outcome. Uncertainties remain from potential late-day convective development or slight forecast revisions in afternoon model runs, which could cap the reading at 33–34°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service forecasts for New York City on August 15, 2026, project a daytime high near 82–84 °F under sunny skies with light southerly flow, aligning closely with the long-term Central Park normal of 84 °F. Recent model runs and observational data from NOAA show no significant warm-air advection or clear-sky amplification that would push readings into the upper 80s, keeping the 84–85 °F bin at near-certainty in trader pricing. This market-implied odds reflect the consensus of multiple NWS guidance products issued on the morning of the 15th. A realistic shift would require an unforecasted late-day surge in insolation or a rapid change in boundary-layer moisture, both of which remain low-probability given stable synoptic conditions.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 16 Aug '26.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from agencies like the German Weather Service and European models show Munich experiencing peak temperatures in the low 30s Celsius on August 16, driven by daytime heating under partly cloudy skies, light southerly flow, and limited cloud cover or showers that moderate but do not suppress maxima. This aligns with the market’s heaviest trading around 30–32 °C, as traders weigh model consensus against observed trends that have run slightly warmer than the August climatological average of 23–25 °C. Afternoon observations and updated runs will refine exact peaks before resolution, with any late-day cooling or convective activity the main variables that could shift outcomes within the narrow 30–32 °C band.

Recent ensemble runs show modest spread due to variable boundary-layer moisture and possible afternoon cloud build-up, keeping 82–87°F ranges dominant while capping odds above 88°F below 20%. Traders are monitoring the next NWS forecast update for any shifts in steering patterns or dew-point trends.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Strong Pacific High pressure extending over Honshu is sustaining above-normal temperatures across eastern Japan in mid-August 2026, with Tokyo highs typically reaching 30–33 °C under mostly clear to partly cloudy skies.** The Japan Meteorological Agency’s seasonal outlook attributes this to an intensified subtropical ridge after the Baiu front’s retreat, reducing cloud cover and enhancing daytime solar heating while high humidity limits nighttime cooling. Short-range guidance for 17–19 August shows maximum temperatures hovering near 32–33 °C, consistent with the historical late-summer climatology of 30–32 °C and recent observations of 29–32 °C.  

Market-implied odds clustered evenly across 28–31 °C reflect model spread in exact cloud timing, boundary-layer mixing, and urban-heat-island amplification at the official observation site. Small probabilities assigned to 32 °C or higher acknowledge the potential for brief clear spells or stronger subsidence, while the tail risk below 28 °C remains low absent an unexpected frontal passage. Updated JMA and global model runs over the next 48 hours will be the primary catalysts for any shift in trader positioning ahead of resolution.

Small probabilities assigned to 32 °C or higher acknowledge the potential for brief clear spells or stronger subsidence, while the tail risk below 28 °C remains low absent an unexpected frontal passage. Updated JMA and global model runs over the next 48 hours will be the primary catalysts for any shift in trader positioning ahead of resolution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 18 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current numerical weather models from sources like the Japan Meteorological Agency and international centers indicate Tokyo's August 18 high will likely fall between 30–33°C, driven by persistent influence of the strengthened Pacific High promoting subsidence, clear to partly cloudy skies, and above-normal seasonal temperatures across Honshu. Key differentiators among leading outcomes include afternoon cloud build-up or scattered showers that could cap peaks near 30–31°C versus stronger insolation and urban heat island effects pushing toward 32–33°C; light winds and high humidity (typically 70–80%) limit rapid cooling while sea breezes from Tokyo Bay may moderate coastal readings. With the market closely split, traders are weighing the latest model runs and any short-term adjustments to moisture or steering flow ahead of the August 18 observation window.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office forecasts for London on August 16 project a daytime maximum of 25–27°C under partly cloudy skies with light northwesterly winds and limited sunshine, following the dissipation of an earlier heat dome that drove mid-August peaks above 34°C. These conditions, including moderate humidity and a 20–30% rain chance later in the day, align with the market's strong emphasis on 25°C (46%) and 26°C (34%) as the most probable highs, while capping upside risk for 27°C or above at just 6.7% combined. Historical late-summer baselines around 22°C provide context, but updated model runs favoring stabilization in the mid-20s have reinforced trader consensus on these narrow outcomes ahead of final observational confirmation.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance and ensemble forecasts point to a moderating Atlantic flow replacing the mid-August heat dome, with London maxima likely peaking near 24–26°C on the 18th amid increasing cloud and scattered showers. This shift from the 36–38°C peaks recorded earlier in the week has compressed market-implied probabilities around 24–25°C while leaving room for variance driven by exact timing of frontal passages, boundary-layer mixing, and urban heat-island effects. Model spreads remain notable because small changes in low-level wind direction or insolation can shift the daily high by 2–3°C; traders are therefore weighting the most recent high-resolution runs and the next Met Office update as the key near-term catalysts.

This aligns closely with the market’s leading outcomes (26°C at 40.5%, 27°C at 27.5%, 25°C at 20.5%), reflecting trader assessment of ensemble model consensus and typical post-heatwave moderation. After several days of above-normal warmth driven by southerly flow and clear skies, increasing cloud and a shift toward more typical late-summer Atlantic influence are expected to limit further intensification.  

August climatology for London centers on highs near 22°C, so current conditions remain elevated but not extreme; any last-minute clearing could push readings toward 28°C, while thicker cloud or showers would favor 25–26°C. Resolution will hinge on the official Met Office observation for the day, with the narrow spread among the top three outcomes indicating high confidence that temperatures will settle near the seasonal upper range without reaching heatwave thresholds.
